ratings_why.fun: Watching Fruits pay in order and the back row fatten as the front dies is satisfying, but the per-turn change-making is more arithmetic than spectacle.
ratings_why.distinct: Fruit's fixed-lump, reading-order spending is fresh; the rest (a death counter, deathrattle Spores, death-buffs) is the familiar undead shape with a third hero-frame counter.

verdict_why: The last unclear cards (Abbess, Inkcap, Button) now read cleanly; what is left are ideas that would make it different, not better.

points.text: The Fruit order is only readable with a start-of-turn preview showing which Fruits fire and what is left; treat that preview as part of the tribe, not a later UI nicety.
Button Mushroom's line about Bootlace is a rules note for another card; move it to Bootlace's reminder text so the Tier 1 card reads in one glance.
Hired Mute turns every sale into Compost with no opt-out, which the plays text frames as a choice; a 'you may' wording would make the gold-or-Compost decision the card promises.
Litter Acre Sexton spends the pile on its own mid-fight; a floor like 'while you have more than 2' would let hoarders read what Ashcake and next turn's Fruits will see.
Warden Amanita is the best flavour on the board (the undertaker who caused the death); naming a tie-break for least Health would let players place for her on purpose.

standouts.why: Clerk Inkcap shrinks as he writes the Register and dies of it: the lore is the mechanic, and it reads at a glance.
Bellows Puffwell's 'Fruit 6, repeated while you can pay' is one clear line that makes slot order a real decision.
Old Fingers burying a neighbour for 4 Compost is simple, flavourful and turns junk into fuel.

weakest.why: Dewdrop Bonnet is a plain interest card with a fiddly '1 for every 2, up to 5' rule and little fungus feel.
Three-Rain Mourner is a bare doubler; the name carries the lore while the text is generic.
Wake-Feast Cook's 'random unit behind it' needs the diagonal links in your head and can waste growth on a Spore.

flags.note: Bootlace with Puffwell and the Mourner is the tribe's biggest roll, as the design itself says.
No tie-break when two units share the least Health.
